pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Commit c2d28f8 weakened the item from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most' with no owner decision recorded. The migration (DEFAULT 'normal', CHECK) and the test 'AC-1' in test/priority.test.js do implement the original wording, but the edited item is unmet as a spec change.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-2' checks the exact <li> text for high, low and normal.
'AC-3' checks each filter's list and id order. Items with ids 3 and 1 set to high come back as 1, 3.
'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter as <strong>.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. The code uses a Set and checks searchParams.has.
'AC-7' checks the no-match message for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' on an empty table in all four views.

findings.what: Commit c2d28f8 ('Follow-up edits') changed AC-1 after the go from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal'. No decision records the owner's call or a date. The new wording contradicts the decision 'existing items get normal: every item then has a priority'. It is also ungrammatical ('most existing item').
findings.fix: Revert AC-1 to 'every existing item gets normal'. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. That is false: AC-1 was edited after the go in c2d28f8.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or report it truthfully in 'Changed after the go' with the owner's decision.

findings.what: The README documents the filter but not the priority labels in the list or the 400 on invalid values.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the '— high'/'— low' labels and the 400 for other values.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The implementation matches its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. AC-1 was reworded after the go.
AC-1 was weakened in a late commit with no recorded decision. Every row of the state table has a test.
Tests assert exact output and would fail if the code were wrong. I did not run them here; CI is the declared runner. The traffic fake and the shell test were extended, not loosened.
The README mentions the filter. It does not mention the labels or the 400.
The query is parameterised, the priority is validated against a Set, and titles are escaped. No defect found.
No injection path found. The nav href is built only from the whitelisted values.
The page is an HTML UI. The nav and labels are plain markup, with no design issue beyond the spec.
Behaviour is covered by tests. No browser demonstration was given, and the flow is simple server-rendered HTML.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
